theater: 荊湖江陵、朗州與襄樊一線

battle.name: 荊湖之戰
battle.theater: 荊湖江陵、朗州與襄樊一線
battle.brief: 建隆四年（963）正月起，宋太祖趙匡胤以先荊南、後湖南之序平定荊湖，江陵、朗州相繼請降；同年冬南唐襲取後蜀的襄、樊，次年為宋軍收復。卡面的羅馬重步兵在此作對照：宋軍同樣不靠攻城硬拼，而是靠重裝步卒的編制、水路補給與降兵收編取勝。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 建隆四年（963）的荊湖戰事，實質上是一場由趙匡胤主持、針對江南兩片割據地盤的併吞，而不是兩軍在野外交鋒。北方一邊是新建的北宋：趙匡胤前一年受周恭帝禪讓即位，禁軍與殿衛諸軍握在中央手中，宿將如慕容延釗、李處仁、潘美各領一路兵馬；此時北伐契丹失利未久，朝廷對北方只取守勢，把能用的兵力全部壓向南方。第一個目標是荊南，即南平高氏的政權：其主高保衡在位不過數年，國土控江陵、鼎、澧、夔、峽五州，扼漢水與長江之交，上可蔽巴蜀，下可壓江淮；高氏夾在後蜀與南唐之間，向來稱臣於強鄰而無尺寸之功。第二個目標是湖南，即楚地：周行逢死後其子周保權嗣位，部將張勳、周清位各擁兵自重，潭、朗、衡諸州自相攻殺，號稱精銳的楚軍其實已無主帥可言。西北一邊是後蜀孟氏：南唐於同年冬出兵，攻入後蜀的襄州、樊州，把荊湖的西口搶在手中；南唐主李昪則藉口荊南已下，圖謀由江陵溯漢水西上，兩面夾擊後蜀與荊南。總之，這一戰的交戰方，是一個新生的中原王朝、兩個互相消耗的南方小國、一個趁火打劫的長江政權，以及一個被捲入荊襄爭端的蜀國。
countriesEn: The Jinghu campaign of Jianlong 4 (963) was in truth an annexation directed by Zhao Kuangyin against two southern enclaves rather than a collision of two armies in the open field. On the northern side stood the newly founded Northern Song: Zhao Kuangyin had taken the abdication from the child emperor of Later Zhou the year before, the imperial guard and the palace armies were held directly by the centre, and experienced commanders such as Murong Yanzhao, Li Churen and Pan Mei each led a column. The northern expeditions against the Khitan had recently failed, the court took a defensive posture on that front, and every usable man was pushed south. The first objective was Jingnan, the regime of the Gao family of Nanping. Its ruler, Gao Baoheng, had reigned only a few years; the state held the five prefectures of Jiangling, Ding, Li, Ku and Xia, straddled the meeting of the Han River and the Yangtze, could shelter Ba-Shu above it and press the Jiang-Huai below it, and lay between Later Shu and Southern Tang, paying homage to whichever neighbour was stronger while winning nothing for itself. The second objective was Hunan, the old country of Chu. After Zhou Xingfeng died his son Zhou Baoquan succeeded him, but commanders such as Zhang Xun and Zhou Qingwei each held troops of their own, and the prefectures of Tan, Lang and Heng fought one another; the Chu army, long famed as elite, in truth no longer had a commander. In the northwest stood Later Shu under Meng Chang: Southern Tang marched out that winter and seized the prefectures of Xiang and Fan from Later Shu, taking the western mouth of Jinghu into its own hands. Southern Tang under Li Bian, citing the fall of Jingnan, aimed to move up the Han River from Jiangling and squeeze Shu and Jingnan from two sides. In sum the belligerents were a new Central Plain dynasty, two mutually exhausted southern principalities, a Yangtze government seizing its chance, and a Shu state dragged into the contest over Jing and Xiang.
people: 留下姓名的，多在宋廷一方。趙匡胤是這場戰爭真正的主宰：他定下「先荊南、後湖南」的次序，又定下不急於大舉用兵的方針。慕容延釗原為後周宿將，降宋後是最受信任的方面之臣，攻荊南、平湖南、收復襄樊，役後封南平郡王，史稱南平王；李處仁與潘美（潘仲詢）各當一路，以宿將統禁軍、帥鄉兵的形式出動。宰相趙普在朝中謀主，荊湖既平、江南在手，便乘勢請打通江淮運道，把湖南的米糧納入京師供應，又主張對新附之地「量人力、寬賦斂」，以免重蹈晉末唐初的急徵。對面的荊南主高保衡面對的是無兵可戰的局面：他既無力拒宋，也不敢拒唐，最後只能奉表稱臣，以保家族富貴。湖南那邊更有故事：楚主周保權年幼，兵權落在朗州團練使張勳與衡州刺史周清位手上；宋軍入湘，張勳降而復叛，藉復舊怨起兵，兵鋒一度直指朗州，最後仍為宋軍所平。西北的後蜀主孟昶，眼看南唐奪去襄樊而無力反攻，只能坐視荊湖的門戶洞開。史料對南唐一方的記載較為零碎，僅見林仁肇、邊鎬等將領的名字，具體分兵與攻城次第各書所載互有出入。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive are mostly on the Song side. Zhao Kuangyin was the real master of this war: he fixed the order, first Jingnan then Hunan, and he fixed the policy of not rushing into a general campaign. Murong Yanzhao had been a veteran of Later Zhou and became one of the most trusted of the Song's front commanders; he took Jingnan, settled Hunan, recovered Xiang and Fan, and was enfeoffed afterwards as Prince of Nanping, whence the name by which history knows him. Li Churen and Pan Mei, also known as Pan Zhongxun, each took a route of their own, moving as experienced commanders of the imperial guard with the local levies in support. The chancellor Zhao Pu was the mind at court: once Jinghu and the lands south of the river were in hand, he pressed for the waterways of the Jiang-Huai to be opened up, so that the rice of Hunan might be carried to the capital, and he urged that the new territories be measured for manpower and their taxes eased, so as not to repeat the frantic levies of the late Jin and early Tang. Gao Baoheng of Jingnan faced a situation in which he had no soldiers to fight with: he could not resist the Song and dared not resist Southern Tang either, and in the end could only present a memorial of submission in order to keep his family and his wealth. Hunan supplies a stranger story. The lord of Chu, Zhou Baoquan, was a boy, and the military power lay with Zhang Xun, military training commissioner of Lang prefecture, and Zhou Qingwei, military governor of Heng prefecture; when the Song army entered Hunan, Zhang Xun surrendered, then rose again in arms on the pretext of avenging old wrongs, driving his spearhead as far as the city of Lang, and was finally put down by the Song. In the northwest, Meng Chang of Later Shu watched Southern Tang take Xiang and Fan and could not answer with a counterstroke, and could only sit and see the door of Jinghu stand open. The record for the Southern Tang side is fragmentary, preserving little beyond the names of commanders such as Lin Renzhao and Bian Gao; the details of how the columns were distributed and how the sieges were conducted differ from book to book.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬重步兵，是拿來對照這場戰爭的兵制的。羅馬重步兵以分段鎧甲配重盾，靠的是方陣紀律、充足兵源與穩定的補給線；同樣的道理放到建隆四年的荊湖，看得更清楚。荊南與湖南的守軍以步卒為主，披札甲、持長槍與唐式橫刀，士卒多不習新戰；宋軍這邊，禁軍中的重裝步卒執大盾與長柄刀，配長槍手、弩手、弓手成列，攻城則用雲梯、撞竿、木鴞與望樓，投石砲用於壓制城頭與水寨。守方也非全無準備：江陵一帶城垣外築羊馬牆、置拒馬、掘陷坑，朗州城據沅水之旁，水寨與村柵層層分置，弩手居高臨下覆蓋江面。真正決定糧道的是船：從汴京經汴河、淮水、漢水到江陵，水運數千里；自長沙溯湘水入洞庭，再東下長江至江陵，舟行旬日可達，糧秣主力走水路，這正是羅馬重步兵那句戰力靠補充兵源與補給線的翻版。而補充在此還有第二重意思：宋軍不僅補充糧草，還要補充人，收編降卒、接管州縣、接收沿路的糧場與榷場。火藥武器這時已出現在宋軍的裝備序列中，但這場戰役裡真正起作用的是冷兵器與攻城器械，火器在各書記載中只見零星提及，至於形制細節，諸說並存。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card is here to throw light on the military system of this war. The legionary fought in segmented armour with a heavy shield, and what carried him was the discipline of the square, a steady flow of replacements and an unbroken line of supply. The same logic is far plainer when it is set against Jinghu in Jianlong 4. The garrison troops of Jingnan and Hunan were infantry: clad in lamellar armour, carrying long spears and Tang-style swords, and mostly unaccustomed to fresh fighting. On the Song side the heavy infantry of the imperial guard carried large shields and long-handled blades, formed up with spear-men, crossbowmen and bowmen, and for the attack brought scaling ladders, battering poles, wooden towers and observation platforms, with stone throwers used to pin the walls and the water stockades. The defenders were not wholly unprepared either: outside the walls of the Jiangling region stood chevaux-de-frise, spiked barriers and pits, while the city of Lang stood beside the Yuan River with its water forts and village stockades disposed in layers, crossbowmen on the heights sweeping the river below. What really decided the grain line was the boat. From Bianjing by the Bian Canal, the Huai and the Han to Jiangling was a water haul of several thousand li; from Changsha up the Xiang into Dongting and then down the Yangtze to Jiangling was some eight or nine hundred li, a matter of ten days by river, and the bulk of the grain went that way. This is the very translation of the line on the card about the Roman strength resting on replacements and supply rather than on armour. And here replenishment had a second sense as well: the Song had to replenish men as well as grain, registering the surrendered soldiers, taking over the prefectures and counties, and absorbing the granaries and the customs markets along the route. Powder weapons had already entered the Song inventory by this time, but what actually did the work in this campaign were cold steel and siege engines; powder devices appear only in scattered mentions in the histories, and their forms are a matter of conflicting accounts.
tactics: 荊湖的戰法，由水陸地理決定。趙匡胤先用兵威，再用招撫：他知道荊南與楚都是小國，小國最怕的不是敗，而是分而治之，所以自建隆四年正月起，先遣使宣撫、封爵許官，同時派兵壓境，讓對方在體面地降與玉石俱焚之間做選擇。第一路兵自北沿漢水南下，指向江陵，沿途先取外圍水寨與村柵，再合圍州城；另一路由潭州方向溯湘水而上，指向朗州，水軍居中，步軍沿岸，樓船與蒙衝隨行。攻朗州時，辦法是不急著硬攻：先斷張勳、周清位之間的聯繫，再以招撫分化楚軍，兵鋒指向朗州而糧草線指向潭州，等叛軍自己內訌。攻城序列是宋初最典型的樣子：先以砲石壓制城頭與水寨，弩手覆蓋城牆，步卒持大盾結陣抵近，撞竿與雲梯同時上；守方一旦外援不至，糧道一斷，城中先亂。宋廷在荊湖還有一步不常見的動作：在受降之後，並未把降卒全部遣散，而是分籍編入禁軍與各路廂軍，這與羅馬兵制中補充兵源的做法是同一套邏輯，只是宋人做得更急、更粗。羅馬重步兵那種分段鎧甲加方盾的正面衝撞，在江陵與朗州的城頭前反而用不上；用得上的是盾、槍、砲，以及水寨與城垣之間的配合。
tacticsEn: The way this war was fought was dictated by the water and the land. Zhao Kuangyin showed the sword first and the amnesty afterwards: he knew that Jingnan and Chu were small states, and what small states fear is not defeat but division, so from the first month of Jianlong 4 he sent envoys to proclaim clemency and to promise ranks and titles, while at the same time pressing troops against the frontier, leaving the other side to choose between an honourable surrender and the destruction of both stone and jade. The first column moved south along the Han River and aimed at Jiangling, clearing the outer water forts and village stockades on the way before closing around the prefectural city. The other moved up the Xiang River from the direction of Tanzhou, aimed at Lang, with the flotilla in the middle, infantry along the banks, tower ships and light covered boats in company. In the attack on Lang the method was not to hurry at the walls: first to sever the connection between Zhang Xun and Zhou Qingwei, then to use amnesty to split the Chu army, pointing the spearhead at Lang while the grain line was pointed at Tanzhou, and to wait for the rebels to consume one another. The order of assault was the most typical of the early Song: stone throwers first, to pin the walls and the water forts; crossbowmen covering the curtain wall; infantry with large shields closing in in formation; battering poles and scaling ladders going up together. Once the defender received no relief and the grain line was cut, the city began to break from within. The Song court also took an unusual step in Jinghu: after the surrenders it did not disperse the surrendered soldiers but enrolled them by register into the imperial guard and the regional levies, which is the same logic as the Roman replenishment of ranks, only carried out by the Song with more haste and less care. The frontal charge of the Roman legionary, segmented armour and square shields, was of no use against the walls of Jiangling and Lang; what was of use was the shield, the spear, the stone thrower, and the working of the water forts against the city walls.
data: 可以核的數字不多，但有幾項相當硬。時間線是：建隆四年（963）正月，宋廷發兵平荊湖；同年春，荊南與湖南相繼請降；同年冬，南唐出師攻取後蜀的襄州、樊州；次年（964）正月起，宋軍南下收復襄樊，張勳之亂亦於此際平定。疆域上，荊南領江陵、鼎、澧、夔、峽五州，疆域大致在今湖北荊州、宜昌一帶及湖南西部；湖南即楚地，領州不下十餘處，中心在潭州與朗州。距離與水路是這場戰爭的關鍵數字：汴京至江陵，陸路約一千二百里，水路經汴河、淮水、漢水轉運；長沙至江陵，溯湘水入洞庭再東下，約八九百里，舟行旬日可達，糧秣主力走水路。兵力方面，各書多以概數說話：荊南號稱帶甲十萬，實則老弱居半；楚軍向來被稱為精銳，周行逢死後則兵無主帥；宋軍出動的是禁軍加各路鄉兵，數目同樣只宜作量級看待。傷亡方面，正面大戰極少，陣亡數目不見於史冊，損耗主要來自收編與平叛的零星衝突。財政上的收穫有籍可查：朝廷於江陵置榷場，抽鹽榷酒，所得以十萬計，各書所載數目互有出入，只可作量級看。
dataEn: The arithmetic that can be checked is not large, but a few items are hard. The timeline runs like this: in the first month of Jianlong 4 (963) the Song court sent out its armies to settle Jinghu; in the spring of the same year Jingnan and Hunan surrendered in turn; in the winter of the same year Southern Tang marched out and took the prefectures of Xiang and Fan from Later Shu; from the first month of the following year (964) the Song marched south again, recovered Xiang and Fan, and the revolt of Zhang Xun was put down around the same time. In territory: Jingnan held the five prefectures of Jiangling, Ding, Li, Ku and Xia, its lands lying roughly over the Jingzhou and Yichang region of modern Hubei and the west of Hunan; Hunan, the old country of Chu, counted more than ten prefectures, with Tanzhou and Lang as its centres. Distance and water are the decisive numbers of this war. From Bianjing to Jiangling is about twelve hundred li by land, or a water haul through the Bian Canal, the Huai and the Han; from Changsha up the Xiang into Dongting and then down the Yangtze to Jiangling is some eight or nine hundred li, ten days by boat, and the grain moved that way. As to numbers of men, the histories speak in round figures: Jingnan is credited with a hundred thousand men in arms, of whom half were old and weak; the Chu army was long called elite, and after Zhou Xingfeng's death it had no commander at all; the Song force was the imperial guard with the levies of the various circuits added, and its numbers too are best read as orders of magnitude. On losses: there was almost no set-piece fighting, no casualty figures survive in the histories, and the wear fell mainly on the scattered clashes of the recruiting and the putting down of the revolt. The fiscal gain can be traced in the records: the court set up a customs market at Jiangling, drawing salt and levying on wine, with proceeds counted in tens of thousands, though the figures differ from book to book and are good only as an order of magnitude.
cause: 打起來的緣由有三層。最外一層是形勢：陳橋兵變之後，趙匡胤面對的是一個尚未收拾的殘局——北方有契丹壓境，關南未復，中原方鎮雖已多降，江南卻還有南唐、吳越、荊南、楚、後蜀、南漢各自割據；建隆四年朝廷定的方略是先南後北，荊湖是南邊最先要落的兩枚子。第二層是地理與戰略：荊湖扼漢水、長江、湘江三條水路之交，向西可通巴蜀，向東可達江淮。誰控制了江陵與朗州，誰就同時掐住南唐的西面屏障與後蜀的東面出口，長江中游從此完全敞開。何況局勢正在惡化，963年冬南唐已出兵奪走襄樊，等於證明荊湖的外圍門戶會被別人先搶。第三層是荊南與楚自身的崩解。荊南高氏北受後周與新宋的壓力，南受南唐的窺伺，西與後蜀接壤，三面受敵而無一盟友；湖南周氏更不必說，周行逢一死，張勳、周清位各擁兵自重，兩年之內內戰不休，百姓疲於供應，士卒厭戰。趙匡胤判斷的正是這一點：不必打下這兩國，只要讓它們的內部先站不住，兵鋒一到，投降就是最省的辦法。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason behind the fighting. The outermost was the shape of the situation. After the mutiny at Chenqiao, Zhao Kuangyin inherited a mess that was not yet tidied: the Khitan pressed from the north, the lands south of the passes were not recovered, and although most of the Central Plain governors had submitted, the south of the river was still carved up among Southern Tang, Wuyue, Jingnan, Chu, Later Shu and Southern Han. The policy settled in Jianlong 4 was south first and north afterwards, and Jinghu was the pair of pieces on the southern side that had to fall first. The second layer was geography and strategy. Jinghu holds the meeting of the Han, the Yangtze and the Xiang: west to Ba-Shu, east to the Jiang-Huai. Whoever held Jiangling and Lang simultaneously pinched the western screen of Southern Tang and the eastern exit of Later Shu, and the middle Yangtze stood wide open. The position was deteriorating besides: in the winter of 963 Southern Tang had already marched out and taken Xiang and Fan, which proved that the outer door of Jinghu would be seized by somebody else if the Song did not move first. The third layer was the internal collapse of Jingnan and Chu themselves. The Gao family of Jingnan were pressed from the north by Later Zhou and the new Song, spied upon from the south by Southern Tang, and touched Later Shu in the west: surrounded on three sides with not one ally. Hunan was a still weaker case. Once Zhou Xingfeng was dead, Zhang Xun and Zhou Qingwei each held troops of their own, and for two years there was civil war without end; the people were worn out by the levies and the soldiers were tired of fighting. What Zhao Kuangyin judged was precisely this: there was no need to defeat these two states. It was enough to let their insides fail first, and once the spearheads arrived, surrender was the cheapest way out.
impact: 荊湖之役的直接結果，是北宋一次過拿到兩片地：荊南的五州與湖南的十餘州，總計不下二十州之地，兵不血刃。宋廷隨即在江陵與潭州分置節度、轉運之職，後來逐步分立荊湖北路與荊湖南路，江陵的榷場與湖南的米糧從此納入京師的財政與供應；這是先南後北方略中最划算的一筆，也是後來滅南唐、平兩廣、收後蜀時最可靠的後方。第二層影響在戰略上：南唐失去荊襄這道西屏蔽，長江中游再無屏障；後蜀失去東面出口；963年冬南唐冒險攻下的襄、樊，一年之後又回到宋軍手中，兩度易手說明這條通道誰都守不長，唯一的辦法是不讓對手先站上去。第三層影響在作戰方式上：宋初這一套宣撫在先、兵威為輔、封爵安民的辦法，經此一役而定型，日後對南唐、對後蜀、對南漢幾乎照方抓藥，成為北宋統一的標準做法；與此同時，招撫政策的隱患也一併留下，降而復叛的事在湖南、在陝西、在荊北都一再重演，收編不當的舊軍終成往後幾次邊患的伏筆。第四層是對兵器與兵制的啟示：這場戰爭再次說明，靠重裝與正面強攻是拿不到江陵的，能拿到的是水路上的補給、編制上的補充，以及對敵我消耗的判斷。
impactEn: The direct result of the Jinghu campaign was that the Northern Song took two blocks of country at once: the five prefectures of Jingnan and more than ten of Hunan, something like twenty prefectures in all, and scarcely a battle fought. The court straight away established military governorship and transport commissions at Jiangling and Tanzhou, which were later split into the Jinghu North and Jinghu North-plus circuits, so that the customs market at Jiangling and the rice of Hunan entered the finances and the supply of the capital. It was the cheapest bargain of the south-first policy and the most reliable rear for what came afterwards: the destruction of Southern Tang, the reduction of the two Lingnan regions, and the taking of Later Shu. The second layer of effect was strategic. Southern Tang lost the western screen of Jing and Xiang and no longer had any barrier on the middle Yangtze; Later Shu lost its eastern exit; and the prefectures of Xiang and Fan, seized by Southern Tang in a risky gamble in the winter of 963, were back in Song hands a year later. Two changes of owner in a single year showed that nobody could hold that corridor for long, and that the only answer was to refuse to let an opponent stand on it first. The third layer was methodological. The early Song formula of proclamation first, military pressure second, and ennoblement to settle the people was fixed by this campaign and thereafter applied almost unchanged against Southern Tang, Later Shu and Southern Han; it became the standard method of Northern Song unification. At the same time the latent danger of the amnesty policy was left behind with it: men who surrendered and rose again happened again and again in Hunan, in Shaanxi and in northern Jing, and old troops enrolled badly became the seed of later rebellions on the frontier. The fourth layer is a lesson about weapons and military systems. This campaign showed once more that neither heavy armour nor frontal assault would take Jiangling; what took it was supply by water, replenishment in the rolls, and a correct reading of how fast both sides were spending themselves.
result: 點講結果：荊南與湖南都降了，而且降得很快。建隆四年（963）正月發兵，詔令分道，先取江陵，荊南主高保衡奉表稱臣，江陵及鼎、澧、夔、峽諸州入於宋；接著主力南下，指著朗州而來，湖南楚主周保權在部將挾持、朗州將領反覆的情況下請降，潭、朗、衡、郴諸州相繼歸順，荊湖遂平，設官置吏、括戶榷鹽。同一年的冬天，南唐趁宋軍北伐失利之隙，遣將攻入後蜀的襄州、樊州，把荊湖的西口一度奪去；次年（964）正月起宋軍南下，樊、襄相繼歸宋，盤據荊襄的南唐守軍退回江淮，兩度易手的襄樊終於定了下來。留下的尾巴是叛亂：朗州團練使張勳降而復叛，藉復舊怨起兵，一度攻入州城，經宋軍討平，首級送京；湖南自此再無割據的兵勢。最後一筆帳要算在兵器上：卡面上那件羅馬重步兵，雖然並不出現在建隆四年的江陵城下，但它所代表的東西——重裝步卒的編制、可以持續補充的兵源，以及必須不斷運轉的補給線——正是這場戰爭真正的取勝之道。
resultEn: To state the result plainly: Jingnan and Hunan both surrendered, and they surrendered quickly. The armies marched in the first month of Jianlong 4 (963) under separate commissions; Jiangling was taken first, and Gao Baoheng, lord of Jingnan, presented a memorial of submission, and Jiangling with the prefectures of Ding, Li, Ku and Xia passed to the Song. The main force then moved south toward Lang, and Zhou Baoquan, lord of Chu, surrendered while his commanders were quarrelling among themselves and the officers of Lang were changing sides; Tan, Lang, Heng, Chen and the rest followed, and Jinghu was settled, with officials appointed, households registered and salt monopolised. In the winter of the same year Southern Tang, taking advantage of the Song reverse in the north, sent troops into the prefectures of Xiang and Fan of Later Shu and seized the western mouth of Jinghu for a time. From the first month of the following year (964) the Song marched south, Fan and Xiang returned in turn, the Southern Tang forces that had held Jing and Xiang withdrew to the river, and the corridor that had changed hands twice finally settled. The tail left behind was rebellion: Zhang Xun, military training commissioner of Lang, surrendered and then rose again, armed on the pretext of avenging old wrongs, and at one point entered the city itself, until the Song army put him down and his head was sent to the capital; from that time Hunan no longer held any separatist military force. The last account to be settled is one of arms. The Roman legionary on the card did not stand beneath the walls of Jiangling in Jianlong 4, but what it stands for, the organisation of heavily equipped infantry, a flow of replacements that could be sustained, and a line of supply that had to keep turning, is precisely the thing that really won this war.
